provenance.citation: de Kleer, J., & Brown, J. S. (1984). A Qualitative Physics Based on Confluences. Artificial Intelligence, 24(1–3), 7–83.
provenance.locus: Sections 1–3: the pressure-regulator running example; the valve confluence dQ = dP + dA (flow changes with pressure and valve area) and the central observation that the sign sum + ⊕ − is ambiguous, forcing the envisionment to branch into multiple qualitative states.
provenance.notes: The paper's valve confluence is encoded as +p,+a,-q (i.e., [dP] + [dA] − [dQ] = 0). The regulator scenario: pressure rising ([dP] = +) while the regulator closes the valve ([dA] = −). The confluence is then ambiguous in [dQ] — the paper's key point: qualitative physics cannot determine whether flow increases, stays, or decreases, so the envisionment contains exactly the three branches dQ ∈ {+, 0, −}.

input.intent: envision the pressure-regulator valve confluence (de Kleer & Brown 1984)

expected.notes: Exactly three qualitative states, one per [dQ] branch — the paper's ambiguity result.
